item.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
item.description: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.
item.content:encoded:
Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.

(Image credit: Alex Wong)
item.dc:creator: Ava Berger

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.
item.content:encoded:
The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

(Image credit: Ahn Young-joon)

item.title: A new report finds many Chinese provinces are reducing their use of coal
item.description: China is the world's largest emitter of planet-warming pollution. But a new report this week finds the country is transitioning away from fossil fuels including coal.
item.content:encoded: China is the world's largest emitter of planet-warming pollution. But a new report this week finds the country is transitioning away from fossil fuels including coal.

item.title: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
item.description: Heat kills thousands of people across the U.S. every year. The risk is especially high for the millions of Americans who live in manufactured housing like mobile homes and trailers.

item.title: Forecasters sound the alarm over a powerful El Nino climate pattern
item.description: Forecasters expect the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.

item.title: Inside the failed mission to eliminate FEMA
item.description: David Richardson worked to eliminate the country's top disaster agency when he led FEMA last year. Now, he says the administration has abandoned that goal.

item.title: U.N. climate report warns world will soon cross a dangerous threshold
item.description: A new United Nations report finds that the world will soon pass a dangerous threshold for climate warming. Countries had agreed to limit warming to that level to avoid the most extreme impacts.

item.title: Chevron's expansion in Venezuela has implications for the oil industry and the planet
item.description: Chevron is expanding its current operations in Venezuela. The deal expands the company's footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty in Venezuela.

item.description: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

item.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
item.description: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.
